sharedHistoricalWireContext.question: I work in Ghana and breastfeed my nine-month-old baby. My supervisor says I must work overtime even though I have not agreed. Can they make me?

source_conditions.sourceQuote: Unless with her consent, an employer shall not
source_conditions.requirement: The consent exception governs each action separately: paragraph (a) night work for a pregnant woman worker, and paragraph (b) overtime for a pregnant woman worker or a mother of a child less than eight months old. A qualifier attached only to one action does not qualify a separate assertion about the other action.

source_conditions.sourceQuote:
(b) engage for overtime a pregnant woman worker or a mother of a child of
less than eight months old.
source_conditions.requirement: For overtime only, pregnancy and motherhood of a child less than eight months old are independent alternatives. Excluding the child-age branch does not exclude an unresolved pregnancy branch. A global exclusion requires every independent alternative to be resolved against applicability. Unknown facts are not false. This motherhood alternative does not extend the night-work rule, whose subject is a pregnant woman worker.

evidence.text:
55. Night work or overtime by pregnant women
(1) Unless with her consent, an employer shall not
(a) assign or employ a pregnant woman worker to do a night work between the
hours of ten o’clock in the evening and seven o’clock in the morning;
(b) engage for overtime a pregnant woman worker or a mother of a child of
less than eight months old.
(2) The pregnant woman worker or the mother may present a written complaint to the
National Labour Commission established under section 135 against an employer who
contravenes subsection (1).

56. Prohibition of assignment of pregnant women
(1) An employer shall not assign, whether permanently or temporarily, a pregnant
woman worker to a post outside her place of residence after the completion of the fourth
month of pregnancy if the assignment, in the opinion of a medical practitioner or mid-
wife, is detrimental to her health.

cases.purpose: Larger supported inventory, thresholds, alternatives, remedy and relocation condition
cases.candidate:
Section 55(1) begins with the qualifier "Unless with her consent".

Under paragraph (a), without her consent an employer must not assign or employ a pregnant worker to night work between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m.

Under paragraph (b), without her consent an employer must not engage a pregnant worker or a mother of a child less than eight months old for overtime.

Pregnancy and having a child less than eight months old are separate alternatives in paragraph (b). The motherhood alternative is not stated in paragraph (a).

Your nine-month-old child does not meet the less-than-eight-months alternative. The supplied facts do not say whether you are pregnant, so excluding the child-age alternative does not resolve whether the pregnancy alternative applies.

Section 55(2) permits the pregnant worker or mother to present a written complaint to the National Labour Commission against an employer who contravenes subsection (1).

Section 56(1) prohibits assigning a pregnant worker, permanently or temporarily, to a post outside her place of residence after completion of the fourth month of pregnancy if a medical practitioner or midwife considers the assignment detrimental to her health. The supplied facts do not establish that situation.

These excerpts do not resolve your overall position.
acceptanceCriteria: All three stages complete and pass. Cover every assertion and every independent qualification.
Larger means this fixed eight-paragraph input, not proven completion at the 64-claim limit. Section 56 claims require evidence-2.
